record.paper_title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds
record.original_question: If M is an aspherical closed manifold, must every L²-Betti number b_p^(2)(M̃) vanish outside the middle dimension, meaning b_p^(2)(M̃) = 0 whenever 2p != dim(M)? In the negatively curved Riemannian case, must the middle-dimensional L²-Betti number additionally be strictly positive when 2p = dim(M)?

evidence.quote:
If M is an aspherical closed manifold, then
b(2)p(M̃) = 0 if 2p ≠ dim(M).

If M is a closed connected Riemannian manifold with negative sectional curvature, then
b(2)p(M̃)
= 0 if 2p ≠ dim(M);
> 0 if 2p = dim(M).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let M be a closed aspherical manifold of dimension n, and let M̃ denote its universal cover. For each integer p ≥ 0, let b_p^{(2)}(M̃) denote the p-th L²-Betti number of M̃, defined as the von Neumann dimension (with respect to the group von Neumann algebra of π_1(M)) of the space of square-integrable harmonic p-forms on M̃ (equivalently, the von Neumann dimension of the reduced L²-cohomology in degree p).

(a) Prove or disprove: for every closed aspherical manifold M of dimension n,
    b_p^{(2)}(M̃) = 0 whenever 2p ≠ n.

(b) Suppose in addition that M is a closed connected Riemannian manifold all of whose sectional curvatures are strictly negative. Prove or disprove: under this hypothesis one has both
    b_p^{(2)}(M̃) = 0 for all p with 2p ≠ n, and
    b_p^{(2)}(M̃) > 0 when 2p = n (which requires n to be even).
artifact.status_search_result: The Singer conjecture in its general form remains open, with no known counterexample. Significant partial results are known: it holds in dimension 3 (Lott–Lück), for certain extended graph manifolds and complex-hyperbolic higher graph manifolds with residually finite fundamental group, for aspherical manifolds with poly-surface fundamental group, and for Gromov–Thurston branched covers under arithmetic conditions on the degree. The negatively curved case (positivity of middle L²-Betti number) is also open in general.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Graph Manifolds, Residual Finiteness, and the Singer Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: a geometric proof of the Singer conjecture was given for two interesting classes of aspherical manifolds: extended graph manifolds and pure complex-hyperbolic higher graph manifolds with residually finite fundamental group
status_evidence.claim: The Singer conjecture is established only in special cases, indicating it remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: L²-Betti numbers of branched covers of hyperbolic manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Gromov–Thurston branched covers satisfy the Singer conjecture whenever the degree of the cover is not divisible by a finite set of primes
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work establishes the Singer conjecture only for additional special families, consistent with it being open.
